### Investment Memo: NOW (ServiceNow) — 17 November 2026

**Verdict**: BUY — staged, starter size only | Conviction: **Medium**
**Price Target**: $116 (+25% from $92.90), probability-weighted
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months

**Investment Thesis**

ServiceNow is a wide-moat, 20%-growth workflow franchise trading at the cheapest multiple in its public history (~5.8x EV/FY26E sales, ~16.5x reported forward FCF) after a 60% drawdown driven by AI-disruption fear and a cRPO guide-down to 18.5%. The forensic short agent affirmatively cleared the accounts (M-score −2.91, accruals −14.2%, cash conversion 311%) and declined to short at this level — the bear case has already been paid. But the forward-bookings deceleration is real, the balance sheet just swung from net cash to +$6.0B net debt to fund peak-priced M&A, and on SBC-adjusted owner earnings the stock is only fair-to-modestly-undervalued. That mix merits capital at risk at starter size with staged adds — not full conviction.

**The decisive disagreement, flagged:** the entire Strong-Buy-to-Hold dispersion reduces to one number — which FCF to capitalize. Growth uses reported FY26 FCF ~$5.84B (16.5x). Value uses SBC-adjusted owner earnings ~$2.4B (~$97/share, i.e., spot is roughly fair). SBC is 15% of revenue and buybacks have never reduced share count, so I weight Value's method: **adequacy edge, not asymmetry.**

---

**Key Findings by Domain**

- **Macro & Sector**: Macro **unfavourable** — 10Y at 5.12%, a live December hike (~55–60%), USD +3.9% in 8 weeks; ~80% of DCF value is terminal, so the rate-duration channel dominates. Sector **neutral**: enterprise software spend still grows mid-teens, but the market is repricing seat-based licensing (median SaaS EV/Rev 5.7x→3.2x). NOW grows +20.9% vs peer median +17.6% with the group's best margin-expansion record — a premium asset in a de-rating sector.
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: **Medium.** 63% US revenue, no China/Russia exposure. Real exposures: US federal budget/procurement politics, EU sovereignty + AI Act landing on 25.6% of revenue (EMEA), and a near-certain 10b-5 class action post-crash — largely insured, cost is distraction and disclosure credibility, not solvency.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Value**: **Hold, accumulate <$85.** Wide moat (CMDB switching costs, ~98% renewals) but *narrowing for the first time*: GM 77.5%→70.5% in Q3, TTM FCF +4% on +16% revenue. IV $97–144, midpoint ~$115–120. Capital allocation marked down (management 6.5/10): $7.6B debt-funded acquisition, $2.2B of buybacks at 2x today's price.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Growth**: **Strong Buy** (most aggressive on the team). AI ACV $1.0B→$1.7B (+70%), agentic consumption +13x, RPO $29.7B +22%, 680 customers >$5M ACV, Rule of 57. Own estimate: ~8x 2030 FCF if consensus holds. Acknowledges cRPO deceleration as the thesis risk.
- **Quantitative Signals**: **Neutral** with stale inputs. Reported +17.3% momentum **excludes the last 21 sessions (−36%)** — live trend is sharply negative. +23% revision score references a 2030 estimate period. Sharpe 0.085, R² 0.025 — no measurable alpha.
- **Financial Risk**: **Moderate, negative trajectory.** Net debt −$3.9B→+$6.0B in three quarters; net debt/EBITDA 1.75x; goodwill 104% of equity; SBC = ~49% of FCF. Solvency survives even a −20% revenue scenario — the realistic bear case is de-rating + impairment + dilution, not default.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: **HIGH.** June 2026 exploited data-access incident against customer instances; securities investigations with suit likely within 60–90 days; definitional discretion in the cRPO metric (T4C exclusions); GTM leadership departures; **zero insider buying and zero Q3 buyback during a 38% drawdown** — the strongest counter-signal is missing.
- **ESG**: **Average, and not the thesis driver.** Carbon financially immaterial (0.26 t/$M). Governance 6/10 — combined Chair/CEO is the main deduction. The drawdown is an AI/valuation event, not an ESG event.
- **Alternative Data**: **Bearish 1–2 quarters.** Brand search −24% y/y and decaying months before the print; EPS surprise trend +14.7%→−2.0% (first miss); no retail capitulation spike. Guidance: don't front-run "cheap" before the 27 January print.
- **Short / Contrarian View**: **No edge — short rejected.** No fraud signature; receivables growing slower than revenue; the −60% drawdown already repriced the thesis. Re-arm triggers: cRPO <15% cc, GM <76%, NRR disclosure turning negative, impairment.

---

**Bull Case**
- Valuation reset vs. intact franchise: 5.8x FY26E EV/S, ~16.5x reported forward FCF, net-cash-generative, 20% growth, RPO +22% — the de-rating (~60%) overshoots the fundamental deceleration (~200–300bp).
- AI is monetizing, not cannibalizing (so far): AI ACV +70% to a $1.7B target, consumption +13x, large-deal metrics accelerating (19 deals >$5M, +135% y/y). If the April 2026 consumption-pricing transition holds revenue-per-customer, NOW is the governance toll-road on enterprise agents, not a displaced seat vendor.
- Disinflation-shock optionality: if CPI breaks toward ~2.5% by mid-2027, the Fed's September hike reverses, the 10Y retraces toward ~4.2%, and a 20% grower at a trough multiple re-rates 40–60% with no change in fundamentals. Credit (90bp IG) says the catastrophe isn't happening.

**Bear Case**
- cRPO 21.5%→20.5%→**18.5% guided** is the thesis: forward bookings decelerating ~300bp in three quarters, with FY27 consensus (~+18.6%) likely still optimistic. A print <15% cc converts a sentiment story into a structural one.
- Margin reset may be permanent: GM −4.4pp to 70.5%, first EPS miss in seven quarters, inference costs migrating into third-party cloud opex — a consumption model has real marginal cost that the seat model never did.
- SBC treadmill + deteriorating capital allocation: SBC 15% of revenue, share count up despite $1.84B of FY25 buybacks, $6B of new debt funding goodwill now at 104% of equity. On owner earnings the "cheap" multiple is ~27x, not 16x.

**Key Risks**
1. cRPO prints <15% cc or FY27 subscription guide <15% → thesis broken, exit (27 Jan 2027 is the binary).
2. Gross margin <76% in any quarter → structural reset confirmed.
3. Formal DOJ/SEC action on Q3 growth commentary, or a metric-definition change in cRPO → disclosure-credibility event.
4. Goodwill impairment against the $13.6B intangible book; net debt/EBITDA >2.5x.
5. Churn in regulated verticals traceable to the June 2026 security incident.
6. Macro mirror-image: 10Y term premium running to ~6% takes NOW to $65–70 on duration math alone.

**Data caveats:** sell-side consensus PT (~$157) is entirely pre-crash and stale; peer multiples unavailable (screen returned mega-cap semis); quant momentum/vol inputs internally inconsistent — sizing uses realised vol (69%), not beta.

**Portfolio Construction Note** (Strategist)
**Initiate 0.75% now; scale to 1.5%; hard cap 2.5%.** Probability-weighted value $116 (30%×$97 / 45%×$130 / 15%×$144 / 10%×$67). Tranche 2 (+0.50%) at ≤$85 **or** on a 27 Jan print with cRPO ≥18.5% and FY27 guide ≥17%; tranche 3 (+0.25%) on two quarters of FCF re-acceleration plus GM ≥76%. Hard price stop $76 on early tranches; thesis-invalidation triggers above are the primary stop. Correlations to CRM/WDAY/ADBE are 0.68–0.74 — this is application-software beta, not a diversifier; fund partly by trimming a correlated holding and cap aggregate app-software exposure at 8–10%. Trim half at $130; exit or cut to core at $144+. Time stop July 2027. Size for a >40% drawdown, never for beta.

# Portfolio Construction Recommendation — ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW)

**Spot $92.90 (17 Nov 2026) · Mkt cap $97.3bn · EV ~$93bn · 1.047bn diluted shares · 69% realised vol**

### Verification note — conflicts I resolved before sizing
| Conflict | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Net debt: Fin Risk **+$6.0bn** vs vendor ratios implying ~$3.9bn net **cash** vs Growth/Short "$1.3–3bn net cash" | Vendor EV/ratios are computed off the **FY2025** balance sheet (`period_end 2025-12-31`). **Adopt Fin Risk's TTM +$6.0bn net debt / 1.75x EBITDA** — it is the only post-acquisition figure. |
| Momentum **+17.34%** ("positive") | I verified this 12-1 window **excludes the last 21 sessions, which contained −36.1%** ($145.36 → $92.90). Momentum is stale; **live trend is sharply negative.** Signal downgraded. |
| Consensus PT ~$157 (+69%) | All 12 notes are dated **29 Oct** (posted at $110–$150); **none has been marked since the slide to $93.** Low anchor KeyBanc $110. Treat as lagging; unpublished cuts are likely. |
| Quant's "actual price ~$900/sh, 207M shares" | Not supported by this dataset — price series, valuation ratios and cap all reconcile at **$92.90 / 1.047bn / $97.3bn**. I reject that caveat and use this basis. |
| Vol 69% vs beta 0.753 | Internally inconsistent and unresolvable. **Size on realised vol (69%)** — the conservative input. Confirmed max DD −41.6% and five −10%+ gaps in 22 months. |

---

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| Growth | **Strong Buy** | High (most aggressive) | AI ACV $1.0→1.7bn (+70%), Rule of 57, 19 deals >$5M +135%, 5.8x EV/S, 16.5x fwd FCF; stage entries |
| Value | **Hold; accumulate <$85** | Med-High | Wide moat *narrowing*; IV $97–144 (mid ~$115–120); only **18–22% discount vs 25–30% hurdle**; mgmt 6.5/10 |
| Short Analyst | **No edge — reject short** | Med-High | M-score −2.906, accruals −14.2%, cash conversion 311%: **no fraud**; bear case already paid at −60%; re-arm triggers defined |
| Fin Risk | **Moderate, negative trajectory** | High | Debt 3.5x→$8.4bn, net debt/EBITDA 1.75x, goodwill **104% of equity**, GM 77.5%→70.5%, SBC = 49% of FCF, 52% vol |
| Nonfin Risk | **High** | High | June 2026 **exploited data-access incident**; securities investigations (suit likely 60–90d); cRPO "T4C" definitional discretion; GTM departures; **zero insider buying, $0 Q3 buyback** |
| Macro | **Unfavourable** | Med-High | 10Y 5.12%, live Dec hike, USD +3.9%; ~80% of DCF in terminal value; **but much rate damage now priced** |
| Geo Legal | **Medium risk** | Medium | 63% US / 25.6% EMEA, no China/Russia; EU sovereignty + AI Act; near-certain 10b-5 settlement (largely insured) |
| Sector | **Neutral** (NOW position: Strong) | Medium | +20.9% vs peer median +17.6%, 2nd-best margin expansion; but 6.0x EV/S vs 3.2x SaaS median |
| Alt Data | **Bearish, 1–2 quarters** | Medium | Trends −24% y/y, no retail capitulation, surprise trend decayed +14.7%→**−2.0%**; "don't front-run cheap before 27 Jan" |
| Quant | **Neutral** | Low (self-flagged) | Revisions +23.2% (but to a **2030** period), Sharpe 0.085, R² 0.025 → alpha t-stat ~0.8 |
| ESG | **Average / neutral** | Medium | E immaterial (0.26 t/$M); Governance 6/10 (Chair+CEO combined); **not the driver** |

## 2. Consensus Assessment: **SPLIT** (high on facts, low on conclusion)

**Agreed by 9+ agents — treat as established:** (i) business quality is genuinely high (wide moat, 680 customers >$5M ACV, RPO $29.7bn +22%); (ii) **cRPO deceleration 21.5%→20.5%→18.5% guided is real and is the thesis**; (iii) valuation has reset hard but is *not* cheap on GAAP earnings (P/E 55.6); (iv) SBC ~15% of revenue / ~half of FCF is a real cost; (v) 27 Jan 2027 is a live binary.

**The decisive disagreement is a single number: which FCF to capitalize.** Growth uses reported FY26 FCF ~$5.84bn (→ 16.5x). Value's conservative case uses owner earnings $2.4bn after SBC (→ **~$97/share, i.e. spot is roughly fair**). That $5.84bn-vs-$2.4bn gap explains the entire Strong-Buy-to-Hold dispersion. **My resolution: split it and weight toward Value's method** — SBC is cash-equivalent compensation and the buyback has never reduced share count ($1.84bn spent in FY25, shares still +8.0M). On SBC-adjusted economics NOW is **fair-to-modestly-undervalued, not asymmetric.**

**Framework precedence applied:** the fraud veto does **not** trigger — the Short Analyst, the agent built to find it, explicitly cleared the accounts. But **non-financial risk (HIGH) and financial-risk trajectory (deteriorating) override the Growth bull case**, per my rule that risk flags take precedence over valuation enthusiasm. α is not present: the expected gap between price and probability-weighted value is ~25%, which is an *adequacy* edge, not a *compelling* one.

---

## 3. Position Sizing: **Target 1.5% of portfolio; initiate 0.75% now; cap 2.5%**

Probability-weighted value: 30% Conservative $97 · 45% Base $130 · 15% Bull $144 · 10% Bear $67 (macro's 6% 10Y case) = **~$116 EV, +25% vs spot.** A real but modest edge, with parameter uncertainty dominated by the FCF-definition fork.

| Sizing test | Output |
|---|---|
| Framework band (medium conviction **+** multiple risk flags) | 1–3%, treated as 1–2% |
| Kelly (p=0.60, +35%/−25%, b=1.4) | f = 31% → half-Kelly 15.7% — **rejected**: full-sample Kelly with fat tails, five −10% gaps and 0.74 sector correlation is a trap |
| **Vol-budget rule (risk contribution capped at 1.0% of portfolio vol)** | w = 1.0% / 69% = **1.45%** ← binding constraint |

The vol-budget rule and the framework band converge independently at ~1.5%. That is the size.

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

- **Sector concentration:** correlations are **CRM 0.74, WDAY 0.71, ADBE 0.68**, SNOW 0.52, MSFT 0.44. This is **not a diversifier — it is another unit of application-software beta.** Cap aggregate application-software exposure at **8–10%** of the portfolio; fund NOW partly by trimming a correlated holding rather than adding net sector risk.
- **Factor exposure — the worst-timed tilt available:** high-duration growth, negative value (P/E 55.6), high-vol (69%), and now negative momentum — added precisely when the 10Y is 5.12%, a December hike is ~55–60% priced, and the USD is +3.9% in eight weeks. Macro says the rate channel is ~13–17% of the de-rating and already partly paid; that argues for a small position, not zero.
- **Beta lies:** β 0.753 vs 69% realised vol, −41.6% max DD, five double-digit gaps in 22 months. **Size for a >40% peak-to-trough, never for beta.**
- **Correlation to the bear case:** NOW is the market's designated "canary for AI-disruption in software." Holding it alongside other SaaS names creates one thesis, not several.

## 5. Entry Strategy: **Scale in — three tranches, limit orders only**

Do **not** take the full 1.5% at $92.90. The stock is 9% above Value's own hurdle, sell-side targets are stale-and-uncut, Alt Data flags further estimate cuts into 27 Jan, and a 69%-vol name reliably offers better prints.

| Tranche | Size | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| **1 — now** | **0.75%** | At market/limit ≤$94. Establishes exposure to a cleared-fraud, wide-moat franchise at the low end of its 6-month range ($85.44–$158.96) |
| **2 — add** | **0.50%** | EITHER price ≤**$85** (Value's required entry ≈ May-2026 low) **OR** 27 Jan print with cRPO ≥18.5% and FY27 subscription guide ≥17% |
| **3 — complete** | **0.25%** | Two consecutive quarters of FCF growth re-accelerating toward revenue growth **and** gross margin stabilizing ≥76% |

Avoid market orders in the 27 Jan window; use limits 3–5% below spot and let the gap fill you.

## 6. Risk Management Rules

**Stop-loss (price):** hard stop at **$76 (−18% from entry)** on tranches 1–2 only. A tighter stop is unusable at 69% vol — the ATR alone will trip it.

**Thesis invalidation (the primary stop — exit on any one):**
1. **cRPO <15% cc**, or FY27 subscription guide <15% → confirms *structural* not cyclical deceleration (Short's re-arm trigger #1).
2. **Gross margin <76%** in any quarter, or cost-of-revenue growth >25% against revenue <18% → permanent margin reset.
3. **Formal DOJ/SEC subpoena** tied to Q3 growth commentary (Geo Legal's High upgrade).
4. **Goodwill impairment** on the $4.7bn intangible book, or **net debt/EBITDA >2.5x**.
5. Evidence of churn/NRR erosion in a regulated vertical following the June 2026 data-access incident.
6. **SBC/revenue >16%** while buybacks remain net-dilutive.

**Trim triggers:** trim half at **$130** (base case); trim to a core ≤0.5% or exit at **$144+** (bull case). Also trim on any re-rating above **25x forward FCF on an SBC-adjusted basis** — the Growth analyst's 16.5x becomes ~27x on that measure, which is where the multiple stops being a discount.

**Time stop:** if neither cRPO stabilization nor FCF re-acceleration is visible by the **July 2027** print, exit regardless of price.

**Governance watch:** separation of Chair/CEO at the 2027 AGM is a cheap, high-signal positive; continued absence of insider buying and further zero-buyback quarters are soft negatives.

## 7. Final Portfolio Action: **INITIATE — starter position (0.75%), scale to 1.5%**

**Rationale in one line:** a wide-moat, 20%-growth, cash-generative franchise whose fraud risk has been affirmatively cleared and whose multiple has been cut ~60% — but with HIGH non-financial risk, a deteriorating balance-sheet trajectory, a stale-positive momentum signal, unresolved disclosure discretion over its own headline metric, and a binary print ten weeks out. That deserves **money at risk, not full weight.**

**Why not "Pass":** the bear case's own architect (Short Analyst) declines to short at 5.9x EV/S with 311% cash conversion and negative accruals, and Value's *conservative* floor ($97) sits above spot. **Why not "Add" to full size:** the SBC-adjusted multiple (~27x) leaves no asymmetry, 0.68–0.74 correlations make this a sector bet, and 27 Jan can re-price it another 25% either way.

**Upgrade to 2.5% only if:** cRPO prints ≥18.5% with an FY27 guide ≥17%, gross margin holds ≥76%, AND the securities matter is resolved without a metric-definition change.

**Downgrade to zero if:** any single thesis-invalidation trigger in §6 fires — regardless of how cheap it looks.

# Sector Brief — Enterprise Application / Workflow Software
**Target: ServiceNow, Inc. (NYSE: NOW)** | Reference date: 17 Nov 2026 | Price $92.90 · Mkt cap $96.4bn

---

## 1. Sector Overview

Enterprise application software is a large, still-growing but **re-rating** sector. Gartner puts enterprise application software growth at **+14.4% cc in 2026** and the market at **~$725bn by 2029 (12.5% CAGR)**; total IT spending grows **+15% in 2027 to $7.35tn** with AI software reaching **~$298bn by 2027**. Yet pricing power is being repriced by the market: US software equities lost roughly **$2trn of value in early 2026** on fears agentic AI undermines seat-based licensing, and median public-SaaS EV/TTM revenue has compressed from **5.7x → 3.2x** (Q1-26 median 3.1x EV/Rev). The sector is **late-mature in growth terms (mid-teens %, decelerating from 20%+) and mid-cycle in a demand sense, but in an early-stage business-model transition** from seats to consumption/outcome pricing (Gartner: ~40% of enterprise SaaS spend to shift to usage/agent/outcome pricing by 2030). Dispersion is extreme: high-growth AI-levered names (SNOW +29%, DDOG +28%, TEAM +26%) versus de-rated incumbents (CRM +9.6%, ADBE +10.5%).

## 2. Key Tailwinds

- **Durable budget growth**: enterprise app software +14.4% cc in 2026 and IT spend +15% in 2027 — the sector's addressable pool is still expanding faster than GDP, with AI/automation the marginal dollar.
- **Workflow consolidation & vendor consolidation**: platform vendors with a system-of-record (ITSM/ITOM, HR, GRC, CSM) capture share as CIOs cut vendor count — favours NOW, MSFT, CRM over point tools.
- **Monetisation of AI as a priced SKU**: NOW raised its **2026 AI-product ACV target to $1.7bn**; AI is currently *additive* to revenue (Pro Plus / AI Agents), a tailwind into 2027.
- **Margin expansion runway**: peer operating margins have inflected (CRM 14.4%→20.1%, WDAY 2.5%→7.6% over two years), showing the sector can convert growth into leverage — NOW 4.4%→13.7% over five years.

## 3. Key Headwinds

- **Agentic-AI / seat-model disruption**: the single largest overhang. If AI agents replace human seats, per-seat pricing (still the core model for CRM, WDAY, NOW, HUBS) faces volume and price deflation. This, not fundamentals, is driving the de-rating.
- **Growth deceleration & backlog compression**: NOW's **cRPO growth 21.5% → 20.5% → 18.5% guided**, the clearest evidence the sector's forward book is slowing; guidance-driven, not demand-driven, multiple compression is the norm.
- **Multiple compression / valuation reset**: median SaaS EV/Rev down 44% from 5.7x to 3.2x. Even beat-and-raise quarters are punished — NOW fell **26.9% in a day** on a revenue beat.
- **Competitive intensity from below and above**: hyperscalers (MSFT Copilot/Copilot Studio, ORCL) bundling workflow + AI, plus AI-native startups in back-office (per NOW's own commentary on "increasing competition from smaller software companies").

## 4. Peer Comparison Table

Latest fiscal-year YoY revenue growth and margins (GAAP):

| **NOW** | **ServiceNow** | **+20.9%** | **77.5%** | **13.7%** | **+9.3 pts** |

| ADBE | Adobe | +10.5% | 89.3% | 36.6% | +2.4 pts |
| CRM | Salesforce | +9.6% | 77.7% | 20.1% | +5.7 pts |
| **Peer median (10)** | | **+17.6%** | **~78.9%** | **~4.0%** | |

**Read-across:** NOW grows **~3.3 pts faster than the peer median** with *above-median* operating margin and the second-best margin expansion in the group. It is a **premium-growth, high-quality-margin** asset, not a value name. Peer multiples unavailable in this data set — gap noted. NOW's own implied multiple: **$96.4bn cap / ~$16bn FY26E revenue ≈ 6.0x EV/S**, still ~1.9x the 3.2x SaaS median — consistent with a sustained growth premium but far below its 2025 levels.

## 5. Target Company's Competitive Position: **STRONG**

- **Growth leadership**: +20.9% FY25, +20.5% Q3-26, 6-yr revenue CAGR **25.1%** — top decile of mature-cap software. Now #1 in ITSM/ITOM and expanding into HR, legal, procurement, security ops and CRM — increasing TAM per account.
- **Margin trajectory is best-in-class on the "growth + leverage" matrix**: GM steady at **77–79%** (platform pricing power intact) while GAAP op margin went **4.4% → 13.7%** (FY20–FY25). Only MSFT and ADBE combine >75% GM with >10% GAAP op margin at scale.
- **Caveats**: (i) **cRPO deceleration to 18.5%** suggests FY27 revenue growth settles toward the high-teens, in line with the peer set; (ii) seat-based ITSM exposure makes it a *primary target* of the agentic-AI thesis; (iii) trading volatility has been extreme — **−55% from the ~$209 July-2025 high**, **−38.1% in 14 sessions** post-Q3, and a **Pomerantz securities investigation** disclosed 17 Nov 2026 (headline/litigation risk, unproven). Relative share-gain vs CRM/WDAY is clearly positive; vs MSFT it is contested.

## 6. Sector Rating: **NEUTRAL**

Demand fundamentals (mid-teens spending growth, IT budgets +15% in 2027) argue *Attractive*; the pricing-model transition, growth deceleration into the high-teens and unresolved seat-vs-agent economics argue *Unattractive*. Net: **Neutral at the sector level, with strong intra-sector dispersion.** Preference within the sector for platforms with (a) system-of-record stickiness, (b) non-seat revenue mix, and (c) proven margin leverage — NOW screens well on (a) and (c), is mid-pack on (b). Sentiment, not fundamentals, is the near-term driver; the 3.1–3.2x median SaaS multiple and NOW's ~6x imply expectations are already meaningfully reset.

## ServiceNow (NOW) — Geopolitical & Legal Risk Assessment

**Snapshot:** US-domiciled enterprise software (Santa Clara, CA); ~35,000 employees (Sept 2026); FY2025 revenue $13.28B; Q3 2026 revenue $4.11B (+20.5% y/y). Market cap ~$96B. Note: SEC EDGAR direct fetches were blocked (403) and no 10-K was retrievable through the filing tool, so geographic splits below are from secondary aggregators of the FY2025 10-K/Annual Report and are flagged accordingly.

---

### 1. Geographic Risk Map

ServiceNow discloses only three reporting regions — **no country-level revenue split is public**, so country rows below are directional/estimated from regional mix, disclosed office/R&D footprint, and management commentary.

| Geography | Rev exposure | Basis | Risk level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **North America (mostly US)** | **62.9%** ($8.35B FY25) | FY2025 segment disclosure | **Medium** — US federal/public-sector concentration |
| — US Federal & state/local | Not disclosed; described as a top vertical; Q2 2026 revenue benefited from "strong U.S. Federal demand" that pulled forward on-prem subscription revenue | Q2 FY26 earnings release (SEC) | **Medium-High** — budget politics, procurement/price pressure |
| **EMEA** | **25.6%** ($3.40B FY25) | FY2025 segment disclosure | **Medium** — EU sovereignty/AI regulation |
| — UK, Germany, France, Nordics, Benelux (largest) | Not disclosed | World Forum London (Oct 2026), SPP EU program | Medium |
| — Middle East / Africa (in EMEA) | Small, not disclosed | Regional AI datacenter buildout, conflict risk | Medium |
| **Asia-Pacific** | **11.5%** ($1.53B FY25) | FY2025 segment disclosure | **Low-Medium** |
| — Japan, Australia, India, Singapore/Korea | Not disclosed | Office/R&D footprint | Low-Medium |
| **India (delivery, not revenue)** | Cost/headcount, not revenue | 2nd-largest employee base: Hyderabad, Bangalore, Mumbai; Hyderabad R&D centre doubling to ~1,000 seats; India target ~5,000 by 2027 | **Low** — execution/geopolitical tail |
| **China** | Negligible / no meaningful disclosed presence | No China datacenter or go-to-market disclosures found | **Low** |

## 1. Business Quality Assessment — Moat Rating: **WIDE** (narrowing at the margin)

ServiceNow is the system of record for enterprise IT and employee workflow. The moat is built on genuine **switching costs**, not fashion:
